summary:
Per-bank counts: Citadel 8, Goldman 4, Citi 3, Apollo/Slok 1 (16 items, 4 banks/strategists).

Citadel (Scott Rubner's flows desk) dominates: seasonal buy-point framing into the 4-year election cycle, retail disengagement (not capitulation) in AI names, VIXEQ/VIX normalization, rising S&P correlations, Mag 7 leadership, and top-10 concentration near 40% holding up better than the average stock during a rotational (not disorderly) drawdown.

Goldman frames the AI/tech boom against the 2008 bank bubble — balance sheets are stronger this time, but higher capital costs have already de-rated hyperscaler valuations toward the market average, with risk centered on an unsustainable earnings bubble rather than headline valuation. Also flags ex-US outperformance since last year.

Citi stays inflation-focused: breadth still elevated in August, the Fed's only real miss is on inflation (not employment), and higher 10yr yields historically haven't been a death knell for equity returns.

Apollo (Slok) flags a supply-side story: copper discoveries have collapsed just as AI data center buildout surges, setting up a structural squeeze by the 2040s given ~18-year mine lead times.

All items sourced from the same relay window (Sept 19-20) via MikeZaccardi; no cross-account duplicates found; no Neil (@neilksethi/@neilksethinew) tweets present in this collection.

banks.theme: Goldman — tech boom vs. 2008 bank-bubble comparison, capex-driven de-rating, and ex-US outperformance

items.author: MikeZaccardi
items.text:
GS: Today’s tech boom differs from the 2008 bank bubble: tech balance sheets are strong, interest coverage is high, and compute demand outstrips supply. 

Still, a slowdown in profit growth amid higher capital costs could pressure equities across the capex ecosystem.

Tech P/Es: https://t.co/IDtPJdvaTn

items.author: MikeZaccardi
items.text:
GS: The combo of higher cost of capital and greater capital intensity in tech has reduced the value of their future cash flows and triggered a de-rating.

The dominant capex hyperscalers in the US now have a fwd PE ratio close to the market average. https://t.co/ilmZfbqLug
